evidence: Plaut. Capt. 327: damnum praestet facere quam lucrum
Traupman 365: lucrum facere, make a profit
terms.comment: To make a profit, lucrum facere or lucrī facere; to make a loss, damnum facere.

evidence: Publ. N 5: nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere
terms.comment: Gain made by work or business; also the business itself (see industry).

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.6: cum quaestū compendiōque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly gain made by saving (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: wipe off, clear (a table); not “clear a profit”
terms.comment: Traupman: prīmō annō mīlle dollarōs dētergēre, to clear $1000 in the first year. Lewis & Short gives “to wipe off, clean”, and in comedy mēnsam dētergēre, to clear a table (Plaut. Men. 1.1.2), but not the sense of a net gain; we have found no classical instance of it. Making a profit is lucrum facere, or lucrī facere (Cic. Flac. 91).

phrases.latin: est etiam ubi profectō damnum praestet facere quam lucrum
phrases.english: there are times when it is really better to make a loss than a profit

phrases.latin: namque ista subita mē jubet benignitās vigilāre, faciās nē meā culpā lucrum
phrases.english: this sudden kindness tells me to stay awake, so that you don’t make a profit through my fault

phrases.latin: Nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere.
phrases.english: No profit is as safe as saving what you have.

lucrum.against: Traupman lūcrum; Lewis & Short marks the u both long and short
lucrum.html: De Vaan 349, s.v. lucrum: short *lu- is regular from pretonic *lh₂u-. Hor. C. 1.9.14, quem fors diērum cumque dabit, lucrō, puts lu- in a short place of the Alcaic line, where a long vowel could not stand.
